subject.title: [Security] Session hijacking vulnerability due to predictable sequence IDs in gateway client

question: Does controlled testing show that predicting an event `seq` allows a frame to be accepted across unauthenticated, differently authenticated, or separate WebSocket connections?
rationale: Source inspection contradicts the proposed exploit mechanism, but only the security owners should formally resolve a reported gateway trust-boundary claim after controlled testing.

options.title: Reject the reported mechanism
options.body: Confirm that request acceptance remains bound to the authenticated socket and scopes, document the negative test, and close the report as non-exploitable.

options.title: Open a private security repair
options.body: If cross-connection acceptance is reproduced, move the concrete bypass details into the private advisory workflow and repair the actual authentication or routing boundary rather than treating `seq` as a secret.

recommendation.title: Reject the reported mechanism
recommendation.body: Confirm that request acceptance remains bound to the authenticated socket and scopes, document the negative test, and close the report as non-exploitable.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work covers the same gateway authentication, nonce, role, scope, origin, and device-verification boundary.
